The archived V01 §2.4 (archive l.697–716) held the only declaration of item 539's interface — the request's `district`, `key`, `layer`, `boundary`, `seam?`, `context?`, `laid`, `strategy?`, `params?`, `closeup?`, `outlineTemplate?`, `lod` and the result's `mode`, `blocks`, `ways`, `plots`, `buildings`, `greens`, `pins`, `hoodPins`, `places`, `labels`, `seams`, `report`, `districts`, with every field comment (the absence rules, the SKY-F write). The same base comment places `DistrictContext` and `TypedBoundary` at V01 §2.4 (they are V01 §2.3's and §2.5's). The canon homes both records at II.1 (PIPELINE-0642/-0643). Same defect as VPC-14.
issues.required_change: II.1 (item 539) declares both interfaces exactly as archived V01 §2.4 states them — every field and comment, `outlineTemplate?: OutlineTemplateId` "standalone unit runs only", `lod: 'neighbourhood'` "every mode, a unit run's included", `districts` "in partition order — SKY-F writes a sky run's to SkyIsland.districts; [] for refine and replace" — in place of the comment at l.18009–18011, and cites `DistrictContext` as V01 §2.3's and `TypedBoundary` as §2.5's; V01 §2.4's pointer then resolves unchanged.

V02's citations paragraph (l.7) still bounds file g at "102–113".
issues.required_change: V02 writes item 115's part at build depth as new design: (1) V02 §3.2 step 2 — the rung ceiling (V11's ceiling rows by rung, §10.2's shape; §4.2 S10b) applied to the resolved row of a dwelling: at THORP and HAMLET every family but `single`, `L` and `T` (and the row, shelter and base constructions) and the `towers`, `turret` and `gateTower` cells read 0, no court family, no manor-class row unless specified; at VILLAGE the same for every dwelling but the one manor house (V07 §3.8: with a lord or when specified), which alone keeps the grand arrangements; TOWN and above unchanged; (2) "unless specified" (item 115 (c)): a building the dossier names (V08's reading) or one the author places or reshapes (T6, `setMassing`) reads its full row — a default, never a refusal (item 101 R2) — the why provider naming the ceiling and the clerk saying the building exceeds the tier's usual; (3) epochs (item 115 (e)): a building new or rebuilt at an epoch reads the ceiling of the rung it then has, a standing building is never reshaped down; (4) §1b's row for the ceiling's reads, §3.18 (b)'s village row and T-V2-55 read it; (5) a bar (item 115 (f)): rich THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE fixtures at the wealth maximum show no `H`, `U`, court, tower or turret dwelling but the manor, at most one manor and only with a lord or a dossier record, a dossier-named hall at its full design, TOWN and above byte-identical (a no-op pin), priced inside M6a (V02 §8.3); (6) the citations paragraph reads "file g 102–119".

issues.claim: g item 119's V01 part — "their budget sections read the ceiling for one-time waits and keep their interactive budgets" (canon, dated ruling 2026-09-30, J130) — is absent from V01 §6 (l.2974–3003): no ten-second comfort level, progress rule or measured-gain rule; its one-time waits — generation with stage 2, a standalone neighbourhood document's first map, a replace close-up, the stage-2 switch's edit (a whole-document Re-derive from S2 at §12.6's M(B), never bounded at the METROPOLIS cap), the sky unit run at generation and at a raise, a district or outline export — are not held to it, its interactive lines are not declared unchanged, and T-V1-29 measures neither.
issues.required_change: V01 §6 gains item 119's part: its lines stay the targets; every one-time wait stage 2 adds or lengthens (generation with stage 2, a standalone neighbourhood document's first map, a replace close-up, the stage-2 switch's Re-derive from S2, the sky unit run at generation and at a raise, a district or outline export) completes within item 119 (a)'s ten seconds of total time on §12.1's reference hardware at every rung up to the METROPOLIS population cap, shows progress past one second (item 119 (c); V09's progress view) and runs slower than its target only for a recorded measured gain (item 119 (b); V11's `perf.qualitySpend`); the interactive lines — opening a district, its first visible tiles, the surface marks, a hood-pin edit, T8's preview — keep their budgets (item 119 (d)); T-V1-29 gains the clause timing each one-time wait at every rung to the cap against the ten seconds, the switch edit at the METROPOLIS cap among them.

issues.claim: g item 119's V02 part is absent from V02 §6; and V02 §6.4 (l.2970–2974) budgets a METROPOLIS-target glTF / OBJ / CityJSON export at ≤ 10 s in the generation worker with `'asDrawn'` and ≤ 12 s with `'derive'`, has no line at the population cap (≈ 30 000–36 000 buildings), and its fallback only labels `derive` "slow" — against item 119 (a), under which an export is a one-time wait of at most ten seconds from the click to the complete result at every size up to the cap, past which the wait is a failure.
issues.required_change: V02 §6 gains item 119's part: §6.1–§6.5's lines stay the targets; every one-time wait stage 3 adds or lengthens (the massing's share of generation, an export under every `compositions` option, a `derive` pass, a migration of stage-3 fields) completes within item 119 (a)'s ten seconds of total time from the click at every rung up to the population cap, with progress past one second (item 119 (c)) and a slower-than-target step only for a recorded measured gain (item 119 (b)); §6.4's export line is re-budgeted so `'asDrawn'` and `'derive'` each complete inside the ten seconds at the cap, its pre-decided fallback a `derive` that cannot finish inside the ceiling exporting `asDrawn`, reported (never a wait past ten seconds); the interactive lines (`setMassing` ≤ 2 ms, `setComposition` ≤ 1 ms, a neighbourhood click's streamed batches, the `view` tiles) keep their budgets (item 119 (d)); T-V2-22 and T-V2-24 gain the ten-second clause at every rung to the cap.

issues.claim: V01 §3.4.4 (l.1034) lays a precinct ring on "the reservation's outline offset outward by `dBar + w_tpl / 2` (the kernel's `insetRing` with a negative inset)"; base §3.7 *Insets* (l.4088–4090) admits `insetRing` only for a convex face — `E_NON_CONVEX` otherwise, "the caller … unites the face with a `buffer` of its ring for an outward one". A precinct's outline (a close, a castle's claim) is generally non-convex, so the step as written is refused and its outcome is not stated; the kernel rewrite's note 34 addressed this to V01 and it is not closed.
issues.required_change: V01 §3.4.4 states the offset as the kernel does: `insetRing` with the negative inset where the reservation's outline is convex, else the union of the face with a `buffer` of its ring by `dBar + w_tpl / 2` (§3.7 *Insets*), then the three corner-cutting passes and the 48-vertex resampling as now; §3.18 (e)'s spine-series-ring row gains "a non-convex precinct outline → the buffer union" with T-V1-7.

issues.claim: E-27 unified the valley's plan reach as `valleyReach(X, Y, mode)` (V02 §3.7, l.1233–1242) reading a `shed` `Y`'s whole run in both modes; the archived integer form read `Y.halfSpanCm` for every `Y` (archive V02 §3.7), so `facadeBays`' usable run — the bays, the dormers and the lit windows, byte-identical data — changes for a building whose valley ends on a shed. issues.required_change: V02 records the choice as a decision (J-V2.109: `valleyReach` reads a `shed` `Y`'s whole run in both modes over the former integer form's half span, because a single-pitch plane runs from its eave to its high side, so the bays stop where the drawn valley starts; T-V2-54), and the adjudicator confirms it as the ruling E-27 left open; V02 §3.7's "the two expressions disagreed there" then cites J-V2.109.
